en: Rode out for single combat,
The brave diviner saw him,
And at once brought the lion-maned hero
News for Seytek.
Then the diviner
Spoke these words:
“Lion-maned Seytek, hear me;
I have seen a marvel such as this.
In all the world I have never seen
A man of such surpassing terror.
Do not refuse what I say:
To the ravaging monster,
Hero, you granted a term of seven days;
The enraged Sarybai
Is a fearsome calamity such as this.
His lion eyes are blazing,
His overflowing rage is boiling;
He is swollen like a blue tick—
Such is his appearance.
Armed and furious,
Draped in black velvet,
Khan Sarybai rages;
His stare is like a tiger’s.
No man could face
That foul-natured boar;
His roar is like a lion’s.
The ravager who drives the people mad
Seems able to grind them into sand beneath his feet.
No living soul can withstand his wrestling;
Those he meets seem to fall dead.
His cry is like a lion’s;
His strength seems to have overflowed.
Unable to withstand his might,
Khans, common folk, and living creatures
Seem to flee in terrified haste.
Sarybai has ridden out for single combat—
Such is your monster.
He looks ready to slaughter his opponent,
To gnaw apart whoever meets him;
His baleful venom is so great
That he seems ready to swallow anyone he encounters.
Such is the hero’s ferocity.
His figure is like a mountain ridge,
His blue-black hardness is like iron.
When you behold his wrath and venom,
He seems ready to devour the living—
Such is his valor.
Brave Sarybai has come as a warrior;
From the infidel’s fury,
The black earth itself shook.
His destructiveness was beyond counting;
I saw him arrive.
He became an ember burning with spite;
Before the infidel’s imposing form,
The speechless flowing river
Ceased its course and stood still.
No common multitude can stand
Against the enraged infidel.
When he bellows, he kills;
Unless the one Creator alone knows how,
My child, no living human
Can withstand him.
When he charges in fury,
Every living creature
Flees without looking back.
Sarybai, son of a monster—
Such is his savagery.
Father, what a black-hearted swine!
He has fixed his eyes upon the khan;
When they meet in collision,
He will rend him till his life is stilled.
Many champions have fallen before him;
He tore all the honorable people
Like tufts of spring wool.
Because of that ill-fated swine,
That infidel who devastated the nation,
That calamity fallen upon the people,
The host wailed and the khan died;
All who fought him died.
Heroes died in the mounted struggle,
Many mighty wrestlers and lions died.
Our young warriors were destroyed;
Through Sarybai’s terrible violence,
Our finest heroes wept.
The looming ridge was leveled;
Sarybai’s conflict
Became a deed never forgotten.
Fighting on in grief,
Deprived of his great host,
The lone scourge shrieked,
While many stood trembling.
Ready for this conflict,
Sarybai came to single combat;
His victory promised terrible calamity—
Such was his customary way.
Blood burned from his fury,
And his voice drove out men’s souls.
When he appeared directly in single combat,
The heart of any mortal man
Was torn apart at the sight.
Pouring out his wrath, he armed himself,
Like a black camel bull entering the herd;
The ravager came out raging.
Whoever approached that baleful figure
Would see what awaited him, they said;
Any multitude that grappled with him
Would learn their fate, they said.
Against this infidel Sarybai,
They spread turmoil for six months,
Clashing without respite;
Those whose doom had come fell.
“This is utter calamity,”
The white-capped Kyrgyz wept.
The reason for their weeping was this:
When he strained and charged,
He was like a burning plane-tree ember.
The infidel’s violent heaving
Was like an unbreakable host of warriors;
The infidel’s battle cry
Was like a bolt of lightning—
Such was the sight of his form.
Oh, Sarybai, you swine,
A fierce conflict had arisen;
He let none who met him turn back,
But seized and slaughtered them thus—
Such was his manner of fighting.
Against this infidel Sarybai,
They sent scouts to learn his strength;
Unable to face him, many lords died,
And so many valiant heroes perished.
His dreadful fury became overwhelming;
Those who met him were laid flat.
You were a great one, you were a lion;
The pillar of all these people,
You alone were lion-maned Seytek.
Short is the pointed blade,
Scion of a precious lion,
My mirror left by the noble,
My champion desired by the people,
At every sight of you the heart is reassured;
There is no refuge but you.
A challenger has come to dispute with you;
A heroic lion has come to oppose you—
An enemy named Sarybai.
He is the lion who will wrestle you;
God has granted his wish.
Hero, the term you gave Sarybai
Has now expired, he says;
“Hero, my time to wrestle has come,” he says.
The roaring ravager
Has arrived in all his strength.
He has readied his cartridge pouch
And prepared his powder and shot.
His destructive intent is plain;
He has put on armor no bullet can pierce.
He has made ready his ornamented spear;
The six-layered black earth
Seems to smoke from its depths
Beneath the fearsome boar.
Heed the lord’s words:
A warrior has come to wrestle,
An enemy has come to joust,
An enemy has come to fight.
Shouting as he entered the field,
The enemy of old came as your equal.
Before the terrible scourge that has arrived,
Hero, dread has fallen upon my heart.
If the great host now joins battle,
How can its camp remain settled?
Before the torment of that mighty swine,
What will become of the village?
Watching him, I burned with anguish;
I utterly despaired of life.
I looked, understood, and grieved;
Today I have despaired of precious life.
Not Sarybai but a bullet has come,
A rending flood has swept in;
A fierce force, a mighty conflict—
From the infidel’s wrath,
The black earth itself trembles.”
So saying, the diviner
Stood there delivering his news.
The great drum was made of camel hide,
And was three fathoms thick;
Its hide was camel hide,
And when struck once with an axe,
Its booming rolled out upon the road.
Its thunder spread across the earth;
The wrestler struck it when flight threatened.
Yesterday, when the dawn shone clear,
When light broke through the earth,
When the nightingale sang in the forest
And the cuckoo mourned in the mountains,
When the bright dawn broke,
A booming sound was heard.
When the great drum was struck,
Startled to his fly-like soul,
He saddled Kulansur,
And the fated Seytek rose.
The people cried out in tumult,
Raising a clamorous alarm,
Their banners unfurling in splendor:
“The fearsome foe has come to battle!”
All the champions grew excited,
All the lion-maned warriors were stirred;
The army shouted and surged forward.
Wise men surpassing all in judgment
Proclaimed this conflict aloud;
Commanders of ten shouted fiercely,
And the imposing champions,
Broad-chested and wide-breasted,
Declared that their hearts welcomed his coming.
All the champions grew excited,
All the heroes cried out,
All the wrestlers armed themselves.
Sarybai joined the conflict—
Such was his fierce wrath.
When they grappled, no bullet could pierce him;
Their strength was spent and their power gone.
Life fled, wheeling away,
Gnawing at whoever he met,
Sarybay tormented every soul.
Against that swine whose soul is departing,
Let us all fall upon him,
Let us attack together!
Against that infidel who boasts of his strength,
With an uproar that splits the sky,
Let us charge from every side,
Let us shout and level our spears,
Let us make the battle fierce!
Clashing and grappling,
Thrashing one another like autumn wool,
Becoming like hungry lions,
Spilling blood with our bullets,
Reckless of our lives,
Fighting in fury,
Let us unleash boundless havoc.
Let grim calamity become our sport;
With that dog who ravaged the people,
Let us grapple once!
Let us tear at each other without tiring,
And drink our fill of blood.
Whoever faces us,
Let us hew them down with axes,
Thrusting and stabbing with spears,
Let us fulfill every desire,
Let us meet them face-to-face.
Shouting and fighting,
Let us unleash a furious assault.
Let every spear be stained with blood;
If death comes and our days are done,
Let it be at Sarybay’s hands.
Let countless warriors be slain;
Let us behold the worst ordeal.
Sarybay has gone mad with rage;
Let us test ourselves against him.
